sections.heading: the big picture
sections.body:
Attention in the category is consolidating around proof-led creative. The brands gaining share are the ones publishing evidence, not adjectives.

This brief maps where that shift is visible and what to do about it in the next two weeks.

sections.heading: context
sections.body:
Three months ago the feed was dominated by lifestyle framing. Today the top-performing posts open with a number.

That flip happened without any single large account driving it, which suggests audience-side fatigue rather than a copycat wave.

rows.claim: Proof-led hooks outperform lifestyle hooks in this category
rows.evidence: Across the 40 top posts of the window, openers carrying a number averaged roughly twice the engagement of adjective-led openers.

rows.claim: Interest is shifting from brand terms to problem terms
rows.evidence: Search interest for the two leading problem phrases grew through the window while brand-name queries stayed flat.

sections.heading: what this *isn't*
sections.body: This is a 30-day read of one category, not a forecast. The engagement lift is measured on public posts, so paid performance may differ. Treat every number here as a reason to run the two-week test, not as the test's result.
